cells.tense: The care and the seeing are keeping one pace, right here, together.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: When someone tells you what your care did for them, stay in it — hear the whole sentence and don't reach back for the work.
cells.core:
You can tell what matters before you know why, and what you choose to look after shows it. Care and form are doing one job: the thing you keep gets stronger, and none of it is draining you the way it usually does. Nothing here is being forced. You've found the two or three things worth your hands, and you're giving them your hands plainly, as they are.

The one piece missing is small, and it arrives as thanks. Notice who noticed what cost you something. Let an acknowledgment land without picking the work back up to prove it was earned. Release comes when the thing is finished, not when you've convinced the room it was worth the cost. Take it in, and the whole thing is complete.
cells.sheetLine: You know what to tend, and it isn't costing you.
cells.place: standing where the essence is seen before the reasons arrive

cells.tense: You are already tending what hasn't grown, holding a season that hasn't come.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Use something you've already built exactly as it stands — nothing improved, nothing secured after it. Let it be finished for once.
cells.core:
You can tell what matters early, and that's the trouble: the sense of it arrives so soon that your care is already busy with something that hasn't happened. Some part of what you look after has been carried in your head ahead of its time, and care for what's next grips harder than the actual work does. Two demands stay aloft at once, neither allowed to settle.

The strength here is that you can enjoy what you built instead of managing it. Take a finished thing — the meal, the garden, the room you fixed — and stay with it after it is already fine. No improvements. Nothing to secure. The grip eases when your care stops reaching past what's here.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending a season that hasn't come yet.

cells.tense: Your hands still do the work, though the direction it was for has gone quiet.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Stay with what you've already chosen to tend through a stretch of doubt — no outcome asked, no sign required, just the next piece done.
cells.core:
You still look after what you look after. The watering happens, the repair happens, and nothing in you is aimed at it anymore. You keep the thing alive without any sense of where it's going, and the care keeps leaving your hands on schedule while the point of it stays out of view.

This is work that can be done without a direction being visible. Carry on with what you've already chosen — a plant, a project, a person — and ask nothing back from it. No progress, no pull. Direction returns through work that's still there when it decides to, and the surest way not to lose it is to be found still going.
cells.sheetLine: You still tend it. Nothing in you points there anymore.

cells.tense: The looking-after is happening under your hands, and your part in it reads as small.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Do the next quiet piece in front of whoever it's for — no speech, no explanation, no claim after it.
cells.core:
There is care you keep offering that people benefit from without ever seeing where it comes from — the quiet piece that holds something together. In all of that, your name isn't on it. What arrives for other people as how things work, you quietly arrange. The deciding is yours. Applied to yourself, none of it counts as a sacrifice.

The next piece you're about to tuck away, don't tuck it. Work where the person you're doing it for can see your hands move. Let what cost you something be plain without a speech attached. That doesn't need a claim from you — only a hand that stays in sight for one more minute.
cells.sheetLine: You say it's how things work. Your hand is holding it up.
